mutant.description: The join's admission gate and its key discipline, each exercised against the state that should stop them: a registry with ratified_at_commit null must refuse; a part whose id is not VERBATIM a ratified subject_id must land in unjoined rather than being basename-matched or fuzzed into a join.
mutant.expected: an unratified registry refuses outright BEFORE any read or write; near-miss names stay unjoined; a part with two candidates reads AMBIGUOUS, stays unknown and prints both, while the same part with one candidate reads JOINED; and a manifest that is neither the declared pre-fill nor already preserved refuses rather than being written over
mutant.observed: 16 of 42 parts are UNJOINED on exactly that rule, including names a fuzzy matcher would have joined (graph_edges, graph_nodes, cse, code_heat_snap). THE NULL-RAT GATE IS EXERCISED AND ITS ORDERING WAS WRONG WHEN I FIRST CLAIMED IT. I wrote that the arm exits 'before any read or write'; 4.0.0_SA_CRO~X 021147Z read the code and found the manifest loaded ONE LINE ABOVE the gate. The arm did fire and did return 2, so every test passed and the SENTENCE was still false -- an arm returning the right code for the wrong reason. The manifest load and every card read now sit BELOW the gate, and the control is driven through that ordering with the reads TRACED: forcing ratified_at_commit to null gives exit 2 having opened only card_population_registry.v1.json -- manifest UNREAD, cards UNREAD, measured by instrumenting the loader rather than by reading the source and believing it. THE PRESERVATION GATE IS THE THIRD ARM, AND IT WAS FAIL-OPEN. 4.0.0_SA_CRO~X: the re-run branch tested os.path.exists(prior) and nothing else, so a post-fill re-run would announce 'the pre-fill IS already preserved' about a file that had since been replaced, truncated or corrupted -- the only failure it could see was the loud one. A NAME IS NOT AN IDENTITY. The decision is now a pure function that HASHES the preserved file and requires equality to the declared pre-fill, and a TAMPERED-COPY MUTANT drives it through the real preserve_prefill with a post-fill active digest injected: the untampered file proceeds True, a ONE-BYTE flip proceeds False and takes the exit-3 path. Two arms, one byte apart, different states. All three refusal arms are driven from their failing states rather than declared, because an arm that has never been made to fire is a promise, not a control. ON AMBIGUOUS, A DEFECT 4.0.0_SA_CRO~X FOUND AND I HAD MIS-DESCRIBED: the subject index was a DICT, so duplicate subject_ids collapsed before the hit count and the AMBIGUOUS branch was UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION -- its 0 was a property of the data structure, not of the population, and would have read 0 on a registry that DID carry duplicates. I had called it 'not exercised on this population', which was too kind: it could not be exercised on ANY population. Replaced with a multimap. The required two-candidate MUTANT now runs every time, PAIRED WITH ITS SINGLE-CANDIDATE POSITIVE CONTROL on the same subject: the real registry gives that part 1 candidate -> JOINED; a copy of the member list carrying one extra member with the same subject_id gives it 2 -> AMBIGUOUS, both candidates PRINTED and neither picked, with the rest of the population unchanged. THE TWO ARMS DIFFER IN ONE FACT AND RUN THROUGH THE SAME index_members()/classify() AS THE LIVE JOIN -- a control that re-implements the logic it tests only proves the bug can be written twice, and a hand-computed length would have 'passed' against the dict as well. The mutant is a REFUSAL arm, not a print: a run whose mutant fails to reach AMBIGUOUS returns 1. THAT ARM WAS ITSELF EXERCISED rather than declared -- restoring the exact dict-collapse defect in memory drives the run to exit 1 on 'REFUSING: the two-candidate mutant did not reach AMBIGUOUS', so both halves are reachable from different truths. With the branch live, the population's own count is 0 registry subject_ids carrying more than one member -- consistent with the ratified compile's exact-duplicate count of 0, and now a measurement rather than an artifact. The ratified registry bytes were not touched: the injection is into a new list.

determinism.method: the join re-run with --apply against the same ratified registry and the already-filled manifest; every count derived at run time from the artifacts, none typed
determinism.observed: identical on repeat: 26 / 16 / 0 over 42, admitted 23 / not_admitted 3, EMISSION 42, DECLARATION 23/19, L0 PASS, and the SAME re-emitted digest 0cea826d954a82a8. IDEMPOTENT ACROSS THE WRITE, which is the property that matters for a pass that mutates its own input: the second run detects that the active manifest is no longer the pre-fill but that the pre-fill IS already preserved, and declines to re-preserve -- so a re-run cannot overwrite the pre-fill record with a post-fill copy under a pre-fill name. Both reconciliations (admitted + not_admitted == joined; declared + unknown == denominator) are asserted by the runner and its exit code depends on them.
